'''Sukbok Chang''' ({{Korean|hangul=장석복}}; born August 1, 1962) is a South Korean organic chemist. He is a distinguished professor in the Department of Chemistry at [[KAIST|Korea Advanced Institute of Science and Technology]] (KAIST). He is also the director of the [[Institute for Basic Science]] (IBS) Center for Catalytic Hydrocarbon Functionalizations (CCHF). He is the fourth president of IBS and the first to serve in the role after first being a [[principal investigator]] at that institute. 

He was an associate editor on ''[[ACS Catalysis]]'' and has served on the editorial advisory boards of ''[[The Journal of Organic Chemistry]]'', ''[[Journal of the American Chemical Society]]'', and ''[[Accounts of Chemical Research]]''.<ref name=":2019award"/> His major research interest is [[transition metal]] catalyzed [[C-H functionalization|C-H bond functionalization]] for the carbon-carbon bond and carbon-heteroatom bond formation. 

== Career ==
Sukbok Chang received his B.S degree from [[Korea University]] in 1985, and M.S degree from [[KAIST]] in 1987. Then, he joined [[Eric Jacobsen (chemist)|Eric N. Jacobsen]]'s group and received his PhD in 1996 at [[Harvard University]]. He subsequently worked with [[Robert H. Grubbs]] at [[California Institute of Technology|Caltech]] as a postdoctoral fellow from 1996 to 1998. In early 1998, he joined the faculty of [[Ewha Womans University]] as an assistant professor, and moved to KAIST as a full professor in 2002. In 2012, he was selected as a director of the Center for Catalytic Hydrocarbon Functionalizations at the Institute for Basic Science, which is the biggest Korean government funded research institute. He also has been working as an associate editor of the journal ''[[ACS Catalysis]]'' since 2015. In 2023, he was selected to co-run the KAIST Cross Generation Creation Lab, a laboratory designed to continue the know-how of professors about to retire through collaboration with younger professors.<ref>{{cite web |url= https://www.sedaily.com/NewsView/29KFMHVFK9 |title= "학문의 대 잇는다"…KAIST '초세대 협업연구실' 추가 개소 |author= 노현섭 |date=11 January 2023  |website= 서울경제 |publisher= |access-date= 11 January 2023 |quote= |language= Korean}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=https://news.g-enews.com/article/ICT/2023/01/20230111092328731186fbbc3c26_1?md=20230111092556_U |title=KAIST, 초세대 협업연구실 2곳 추가 개소 |author= 여용준 |date=11 January 2023 |website= 글로벌이코노믹 |publisher= |access-date= 11 January 2023 |quote= |language= Korean}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.lecturernews.com/news/articleView.html?idxno=116519 |title= 카이스트 김정호·장석복 교수팀, 학문의 대를 잇는 '초세대 협업연구실' 추가 개소 |author= 한성형 |date=11 January 2023  |website= Korea Lecturer News |publisher= |access-date= 11 January 2023 |quote= |language= Korean}}</ref>

In mid 2026, he was appointed president of the Institute for Basic Science where he will serve a five-year term.<ref>{{cite web |url= https://biz.chosun.com/science-chosun/science/2026/06/04/4OKSDIF6W5CJFBE7HHQY5ECHAY/ |title= IBS 신임 원장에 장석복 카이스트 특훈교수… 첫 내부 연구단장 출신 |last= 홍  |first=아름 |date= 4 June 2026 |website= [[The Chosun Ilbo]] |publisher= |access-date= 2 July 2026 |quote= |language= Korean }}</ref>

== Major contributions ==
Chang's group studies new organic reactions and mechanisms with transition metal catalysis.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://sbchang.kaist.ac.kr|title=Sukbok Chang's group website}}</ref> In particular, his group contributed to the development of "copper catalyzed multicomponent coupling" in the 2000s. Since 2008, his group has focused on C-H functionalization and made a number of contributions.<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Cho|first1=Seung Hwan|last2=Hwang|first2=Seung Jun|last3=Chang|first3=Sukbok|date=July 2008|title=Palladium-Catalyzed C−H Functionalization of PyridineN-Oxides: Highly Selective Alkenylation and Direct Arylation with Unactivated Arenes|journal=Journal of the American Chemical Society|volume=130|issue=29|pages=9254–9256|doi=10.1021/ja8026295|pmid=18582040|issn=0002-7863|url=https://figshare.com/articles/Palladium_Catalyzed_C_H_Functionalization_of_Pyridine_i_N_i_Oxides_Highly_Selective_Alkenylation_and_Direct_Arylation_with_Unactivated_Arenes/2925928|url-access=subscription}}</ref>

=== Copper-catalyzed multicomponent coupling ===
[[File:Sukbok Chang 1.gif|left|474x474px]]
{{clear}}

Cu-catalyzed multicomponent coupling is a notable process developed by Chang's group. In 2005, they published a highly efficient and mild catalytic three component coupling between an alkyne, sulfonyl azide, and amine.<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Bae|first1=Imhyuck|last2=Han|first2=Hoon|last3=Chang|first3=Sukbok|date=February 2005|title=Highly Efficient One-Pot Synthesis ofN-Sulfonylamidines by Cu-Catalyzed Three-Component Coupling of Sulfonyl Azide, Alkyne, and Amine|journal=Journal of the American Chemical Society|volume=127|issue=7|pages=2038–2039|doi=10.1021/ja0432968|pmid=15713069|issn=0002-7863}}</ref> Unlike click chemistry which generates 1,4-triazoles as products, in this case a Cu(I) catalyst, sulfonyl azide and alkyne generate ketenimine intermediate after releasing N2 gas. This electrophilic ketenimine intermediate reacts with amines and to generate asymmetric imines as products. Chang's group also showed water,<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Cho|first1=Seung Hwan|last2=Yoo|first2=Eun Jeong|last3=Bae|first3=Imhyuck|last4=Chang|first4=Sukbok|date=November 2005|title=Copper-Catalyzed Hydrative Amide Synthesis with Terminal Alkyne, Sulfonyl Azide, and Water|journal=Journal of the American Chemical Society|volume=127|issue=46|pages=16046–16047|doi=10.1021/ja056399e|pmid=16287290|issn=0002-7863}}</ref> alcohols,<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Yoo|first1=Eun Jeong|last2=Ahlquist|first2=Mårten|last3=Bae|first3=Imhyuck|last4=Sharpless|first4=K. Barry|last5=Fokin|first5=Valery V.|last6=Chang|first6=Sukbok|date=July 2008|title=Mechanistic Studies on the Cu-Catalyzed Three-Component Reactions of Sulfonyl Azides, 1-Alkynes and Amines, Alcohols, or Water: Dichotomy via a Common Pathway|journal=The Journal of Organic Chemistry|volume=73|issue=14|pages=5520–5528|doi=10.1021/jo800733p|pmid=18557650|issn=0022-3263}}</ref> the C3 position of pyrrole<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Cho|first1=Seung Hwan|last2=Chang|first2=Sukbok|date=2008-03-31|title=Room Temperature Copper-Catalyzed 2-Functionalization of Pyrrole Rings by a Three-Component Coupling Reaction|journal=Angewandte Chemie International Edition|volume=47|issue=15|pages=2836–2839|doi=10.1002/anie.200705940|pmid=18318034|issn=1433-7851}}</ref> and other nucleophiles can be used in this reaction.

=== Rhodium, Iridium-catalyzed C-N bond formation ===
[[File:Sukbok Chang 2.gif|460x460px]]

Rhodium or iridium catalyzed C-H amidation and amination are other achievements of his group. In 2012, his group published rhodium catalyzed intermolecular amidation of arenes using sulfonyl azide as a nitrene precursor.<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Kim|first1=Ji Young|last2=Park|first2=Sae Hume|last3=Ryu|first3=Jaeyune|last4=Cho|first4=Seung Hwan|last5=Kim|first5=Seok Hwan|last6=Chang|first6=Sukbok|date=2012-05-24|title=Rhodium-Catalyzed Intermolecular Amidation of Arenes with Sulfonyl Azides via Chelation-Assisted C–H Bond Activation|journal=Journal of the American Chemical Society|volume=134|issue=22|pages=9110–9113|doi=10.1021/ja303527m|pmid=22624801|issn=0002-7863}}</ref> This reaction generates N2 as the single byproduct, doesn't need external oxidant, has broad substrate scope and high functional group tolerance. Chang's group advanced their work by using different directing groups,<ref>{{Cite journal|date=2012-09-19|title=Graphical Abstract: Angew. Chem. Int. Ed. 39/2012|journal=Angewandte Chemie International Edition|volume=51|issue=39|pages=9709–9721|doi=10.1002/anie.201290068|issn=1433-7851|hdl=2027.42/137365|hdl-access=free}}</ref> different azides<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Shin|first1=Kwangmin|last2=Baek|first2=Yunjung|last3=Chang|first3=Sukbok|date=2013-06-20|title=Direct CH Amination of Arenes with Alkyl Azides under Rhodium Catalysis|journal=Angewandte Chemie International Edition|volume=52|issue=31|pages=8031–8036|doi=10.1002/anie.201302784|pmid=23788328|issn=1433-7851}}</ref> and various substrates.<ref>{{Cite journal|date=2014|title=Rhodium-Catalyzed Direct Amination of Arene C-H Bonds Using Azides as the Nitrogen Source|journal=Organic Syntheses|volume=91|page=52|doi=10.15227/orgsyn.091.0052|issn=0078-6209|doi-access=free}}</ref> They also published that iridium also works well for C-H amidation/amination.<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Lee|first1=Donggun|last2=Kim|first2=Youngchan|last3=Chang|first3=Sukbok|date=2013-10-10|title=Iridium-Catalyzed Direct Arene C–H Bond Amidation with Sulfonyl- and Aryl Azides|journal=The Journal of Organic Chemistry|volume=78|issue=21|pages=11102–11109|doi=10.1021/jo4019683|pmid=24079849|issn=0022-3263|url=https://figshare.com/articles/Iridium_Catalyzed_Direct_Arene_C_H_Bond_Amidation_with_Sulfonyl_and_Aryl_Azides/2361223|url-access=subscription}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Kim|first1=Jinwoo|last2=Chang|first2=Sukbok|date=2014-01-27|title=Iridium-Catalyzed Direct CH Amidation with Weakly Coordinating Carbonyl Directing Groups under Mild Conditions|journal=Angewandte Chemie International Edition|volume=53|issue=8|pages=2203–2207|doi=10.1002/anie.201310544|pmid=24470125|issn=1433-7851}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Kang|first1=Taek|last2=Kim|first2=Youngchan|last3=Lee|first3=Donggun|last4=Wang|first4=Zhen|last5=Chang|first5=Sukbok|date=2014-03-05|title=Iridium-Catalyzed Intermolecular Amidation of sp3 C–H Bonds: Late-Stage Functionalization of an Unactivated Methyl Group|journal=Journal of the American Chemical Society|volume=136|issue=11|pages=4141–4144|doi=10.1021/ja501014b|pmid=24580093|issn=0002-7863}}</ref>
[[File:Sukbok Chang 3.gif|right|frameless|288x288px]]

In 2016, Chang's group discovered new nitrogen sources.<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Park|first1=Yoonsu|last2=Park|first2=Kyung Tae|last3=Kim|first3=Jeung Gon|last4=Chang|first4=Sukbok|date=2015-03-30|title=Mechanistic Studies on the Rh(III)-Mediated Amido Transfer Process Leading to Robust C–H Amination with a New Type of Amidating Reagent|journal=Journal of the American Chemical Society|volume=137|issue=13|pages=4534–4542|doi=10.1021/jacs.5b01324|pmid=25789561|issn=0002-7863}}</ref> Their new nitrene precursor, 1,4,2-dioxazol-5-one, is more convenient to prepare, store and use compared to azides. Moreover, it has a strong affinity to the rhodium or Iridium metal center, and thus gives excellent amidation efficiency.<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Park|first1=Yoonsu|last2=Heo|first2=Joon|last3=Baik|first3=Mu-Hyun|last4=Chang|first4=Sukbok|date=2016-10-13|title=Why is the Ir(III)-Mediated Amido Transfer Much Faster Than the Rh(III)-Mediated Reaction? A Combined Experimental and Computational Study|journal=Journal of the American Chemical Society|volume=138|issue=42|pages=14020–14029|doi=10.1021/jacs.6b08211|pmid=27690406|issn=0002-7863}}</ref> They later published selective formation of gamma-lactams via C-H amidation<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Hong|first1=Seung Youn|last2=Park|first2=Yoonsu|last3=Hwang|first3=Yeongyu|last4=Kim|first4=Yeong Bum|last5=Baik|first5=Mu-Hyun|last6=Chang|first6=Sukbok|date=2018-03-01|title=Selective formation of γ-lactams via C–H amidation enabled by tailored iridium catalysts|journal=Science|volume=359|issue=6379|pages=1016–1021|doi=10.1126/science.aap7503|pmid=29496875|bibcode=2018Sci...359.1016H |issn=0036-8075|doi-access=free}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Park|first1=Yoonsu|last2=Chang|first2=Sukbok|date=2019-02-18|title=Asymmetric formation of γ-lactams via C–H amidation enabled by chiral hydrogen-bond-donor catalysts|journal=Nature Catalysis|volume=2|issue=3|pages=219–227|doi=10.1038/s41929-019-0230-x|s2cid=104461199|issn=2520-1158}}</ref> with this type of nucleophile.
[[File:Sukbok Chang gamma lactam.gif|center|569x569px|Sukbok Chang's gamma lactam synthesis]]
